subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should the incremental session-memory fix be pursued as a fresh current-main implementation, a rescue of the open candidate PR, or intentionally left as full-entry reindex behavior with existing cache/delta controls?
rationale: The remaining choice affects session-state correctness, memory_index schema behavior, source-wide batching, overlap semantics, and whether the conflicting open candidate branch is still worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade and real-behavior proof.

options.title: Rescue the open candidate PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete schema assumptions before further review.

options.title: Reject incremental indexing
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide embedding cache, delta thresholds, and full-entry consistency are preferable to incremental session indexing complexity.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade and real-behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory/session identity and transcript corpus work makes this the best available routing candidate for the design choice.
